title: Immersive virtual reality during pediatric vaccination: a quasi-experimental study of pain, fear, and care experience.
content: Vaccination is a common source of childhood pain and fear and may negatively affect future immunization experiences. Although virtual reality (VR) has shown promise in pediatric needle-related procedures, evidence from routine vaccination in primary care remains limited. To assess preliminary between-group differences in children's self-reported pain and fear during pediatric vaccination, comparing immersive VR with usual care, and to describe acceptability and safety indicators. This quasi-experimental, non-randomized controlled study included 100 child-caregiver dyads from three Portuguese primary care centers: 50 in the VR group and 50 in the usual-care group. The main clinical outcomes, pain and fear, were assessed before and after vaccination using age-appropriate measures. Post-vaccination outcomes were analyzed using baseline-adjusted analyses of covariance. In the VR group, children, caregivers, and nurses rated ease of use and willingness to recommend; nurses recorded VR-related adverse effects. Adjusted post-vaccination pain was lower in the VR group than in the usual-care group (mean difference = -1.94, 95% CI [-2.99, -0.88], p < 0.001), as was fear (mean difference = -0.78, 95% CI [-1.29, -0.27], p = 0.003). Ease-of-use and recommendation ratings were favorable. VR-related adverse effects occurred in 6% of children, were mild and transient, and required no intervention. Immersive VR was associated with lower post-vaccination pain and fear during routine pediatric vaccination in primary care. Favorable VR experience and safety indicators support further evaluation of VR as a complementary nonpharmacological strategy aligned with atraumatic, child- and family-centered nursing care.

title: Logement à Genève: Ces précieux contrats de confiance
content:
Logements à Genève Ces précieux contrats de confiance
Transformer des logements promis à la disparition en habitats temporaires est une solution certes précaire, mais concrète pour de nombreuses personnes.
«En nous proposant cet habitat, ils ont sauvé des vies.» Grâce à un contrat de prêt à usage, onze personnes vivent dans une maison vouée à la destruction. Ces anciennes victimes d’un marchand de sommeil reviennent de loin, elles qui s’étaient retrouvées sans toit, après un incendie.
Ville attractive, Genève est incapable de loger correctement ses habitants les plus vulnérables. Transformer des logements promis à la disparition en habitats temporaires peut être un remède. Certes précaire, mais concret pour de nombreuses personnes.
Alors que les demandes en logements abordables à Genève dépassent la capacité d’accueil, nos élus doivent trouver les moyens de développer ces trop rares solutions.
Ce d’autant plus que les propriétaires en tirent eux aussi des bénéfices: maintenir une présence humaine dans un bien immobilier permet de prévenir des problèmes d’entretien, du vandalisme ou des occupations illégales.
L’ancien conseiller d’État libéral, Claude Haegi – alors responsable du parc immobilier de la Ville – l’avait déjà bien compris et expérimenté au début des années 80! À la grande époque des squats à Genève, le magistrat avait mis en place des solutions boiteuses, mais respectueuses de l’État de droit, qui permirent d’affecter des espaces à une marginalité dans un esprit de respect mutuel. Le contrat de confiance venait de naître.

title: LIC rejects death claim citing ‘non-disclosure’ of hole in heart, man’s father wins Rs 5 lakh
content:
5 min readNew DelhiSep 21, 2026 03:58 PM IST

A Punjab consumer commission has directed the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to pay Rs 5 lakh to the father of a policyholder who died of a heart attack at the age of 30, after finding that the insurer wrongly rejected the death claim on the ground that the deceased had suppressed his pre-existing heart condition.
The LIC claimed that the complainant’s son had a hole in his heart and had undergone an Atrial Septal Defect/Ventricular Septal Defect (ASD/VSD) closure procedure in 2008, but failed to disclose it while applying for the policy.
A bench of president Ashok Kumar Garg and member Tajinder Kaur of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Sri Muktsar Sahib, also ordered the payment of Rs 10,000 as compensation and litigation costs to the father.




“Death claim lodged by the complainant on account of the death of his son has wrongly and illegally been repudiated by the LIC, which constitutes a deficiency in service on their part, and the complainant is entitled to get relief,” said the commission on September 1.
Noting that the insured was 30 years old and in government service, and that he might have got a medical check-up and fitness certificate before joining the service, the commission said, “Even if we presume, even then, that the procedure was done in the year 2008, whereas the insurance policy in question was purchased in April 2022, i.e., after a period of near about 14-15 years, and he had died in August 2023.”
“So, it cannot be taken into consideration that the deceased had purchased the insurance policy with ill will or was having knowledge that he was suffering from a serious ailment before getting the policy in April 2022,” it added.
Father challenges LIC claim rejection
The complainant, being the nominee and father of the policyholder who died of a heart attack in August 2023, filed a complaint against the insurance company seeking directions to pay the insured amount of Rs 5 lakh.
Story continues below this ad
According to the complainant, his son, during his lifetime, obtained an insurance policy in April 2022, having a maturity date in April 2043. The LIC had allegedly assured him that in the event of any mishap, the company would pay Rs 5 lakh to his legal heirs/nominee, who is also the father of the deceased.
After the son died, the father lodged a claim with the insurance company. However, it was rejected in January 2024, alleging that the deceased had suppressed crucial information about a pre-existing heart condition, including an ASD/VSD closure (hole in the heart) and a Fontan procedure (open-heart surgery) allegedly performed in 2008. An appeal against the rejection was also rejected.
The complainant challenged the rejection before the consumer commission, alleging deficiency in service. He argued that the alleged heart procedure had taken place when his son was a minor, more than 14 years before the policy was purchased, and that there was no evidence establishing a connection between that procedure and his son’s death.
Had a hole in his heart: LIC
LIC argued that the complainant’s son had a hole in his heart and had undergone an ASD/VSD closure/Fontan procedure in 2008, but failed to disclose this medical history while applying for the policy.
Story continues below this ad
It was argued that he had answered the health-related questions in the proposal form as “no”, despite allegedly knowing about his chronic heart condition and treatment.
According to LIC, the non-disclosure of his pre-existing heart condition amounted to suppression of crucial facts. Had the condition been disclosed, LIC claimed it would not have issued the insurance coverage.
No medical record shown: Order
The commission found that LIC’s main ground for denying the claim was the alleged suppression of the deceased’s pre-existing heart condition in the proposal form.
“Although the LIC has stated in its repudiation letter dated January 2024 that the insured was suffering from ASD/ VSD closure/ Post Fonton procedure since the year 2008, no such medical record has been placed on file,” the order noted.
Story continues below this ad
It noted that the first proposal form produced by LIC was only two pages long, did not bear the deceased’s signature or the date of submission, raising doubts about its reliability.
Takeaway
This judgment underscored that insurers cannot reject death claims solely on allegations of non-disclosure without producing reliable medical evidence. It also highlights the importance of establishing that an insured knowingly suppressed a material condition, particularly where the alleged treatment occurred years before the policy and the insurer’s proposal-form evidence was found unreliable.
Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states (Punjab helpline: 1800-425-1082) or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.

title: Myanmar win first Asian Games teqball gold
content:
Myanmar win first Asian Games teqball gold
Wai Khin Hnin wins 10-12, 12-8, 12-9 against Indonesia’s Sumaya
NAGOYA:
Myanmar's Wai Khin Hnin on Sunday became the first Asian Games gold medallist in teqball, an acrobatic football-table tennis hybrid making its debut at this year's event in Japan.
Watched by Barcelona and Spain football legend Carles Puyol, Wai Khin Hnin beat Indonesia's Sumaya, who goes by one name, 2-1 in the final to capture the inaugural women's singles title.
Teqball was invented 14 years ago in a garage in Hungary and features players kicking a ball over a curved table, incorporating elements of the southeast Asian sport sepak takraw.
The sport has grown quickly and featured at the 2023 European Games.
Wai Khin Hnin lost the first set of the final but came back to win 10-12, 12-8, 12-9 and claim gold.
"I'm delighted, I'm thankful to my head coach for believing in me and selecting me to play in the women's singles. I believed that I could do it," she said.
"My next goal is to win the gold medal for Myanmar at the 2027 SEA Games."
The competition has seen a diverse range of players vying to become the Asian Games' first teqball medallists.
The Philippines men's team featured three 14-year-olds including Prince Agustin, who lost in the singles bronze-medal match.
Japan were represented by Takahiro Nodomi, who also works as a comedian.
"I played football until high school, gave up, started teqball in my late 30s, and made it to this big stage at 40," he said.
"If the message that 'even old guys can work hard' reached everyone, then I feel I was able to release some 'old guy power'."
Indonesia's Husni Uba represented his country in sepak takraw at four previous Asian Games.
"After I was done with the sepak takraw competition at the 2018 Asian Games I didn't expect to be back again, especially for teqball," said the 44-year-old.

title: Bulog's near-100 percent rice absorption shows commitment: BP BUMN
content:
"BP BUMN appreciates the hard work of everyone at Bulog. This near-100 percent absorption achievement shows Bulog's commitment to standing by farmers," Director of Public Corporation Management at BP BUMN, M Khoerur Roziqin, said in a statement received here on Monday.
Bulog's mandate covers the entire upstream-to-downstream process to ensure the availability and stability of national food supplies throughout the year.
Bulog is considered to have successfully carried out two strategic functions at once, namely absorbing domestic farmers' harvests and distributing food to the public through both price stabilisation programmes and government food aid.
Related news: Bulog sends 1,321 tons of rice to quake-hit NTT
On the procurement side, Bulog has so far absorbed more than 3.9 million tons of rice equivalent, or 99 percent of its 4-million-ton target. The absorption came from 7.7 million tons of dry harvested grain (GKP) and 35,800 tons of rice.
"Every ton of grain absorbed means market and price certainty for farmers, while also strengthening the government's rice reserves," Roziqin said.
On the distribution side, Bulog has so far distributed more than 810,000 tons of rice through the Food Supply and Price Stabilization (SPHP) programme or 98 percent of its 828,000-ton target.
He said the SPHP programme plays an important role in keeping rice prices affordable for consumers.
Related news: Indonesia prepares Rp17 trillion for Q4 rice assistance program
Bulog has also completed the distribution of food assistance for the February-March 2026 period, with a 99.7 percent receipt rate. A total of 662,000 tons of rice and 133,000 liters of cooking oil have been received by food assistance recipients (PBP).
Meanwhile, distribution of food assistance for the July-September 2026 period has reached 682,000 tons or 68.44 percent of the 997,000-ton allocation.
Bulog has once again received a government mandate to distribute food assistance for the October-December 2026 period, with planned distribution of 997,000 tons of rice.
"With strong domestic rice reserves from its absorption efforts, we are confident Bulog can distribute the aid accurately, in the right amount, and on time," Roziqin said.

title: Udayapur Hospital gets services moving again
content:
National
Udayapur Hospital gets services moving again
After years of unreliable service, the hospital is getting key units back up and running as it tackles staffing and financial problems.Bhotraj Rai
Udayapur Hospital sees 400 to 500 patients a day and remains the main public hospital for much of the district. But unreliable services, absentee staff and unstable management had eroded public trust. After nearly two months under new leadership, the hospital is showing early signs of recovery.
Several suspended services have resumed. Two broken dialysis machines are back in operation. Staff attendance is being monitored more closely; managers now meet before the workday begins, and the hospital is working to improve medicine supplies. It is also preparing to introduce electronic medical records.
For acting medical superintendent Santosh Rai, the immediate task was to restore services that had stopped and bring greater discipline to a hospital long troubled by internal disputes and interference.
The Special Newborn Care Unit, which had been closed for a prolonged period, is operating again, Rai said. The hospital has also resumed arterial blood gas and culture-based microbiology testing.
The newborn unit treats babies less than 28 days old. Its closure meant critically ill newborns had to be referred elsewhere. Arterial blood gas testing helps doctors assess critically ill patients, while culture tests identify infections in blood and urine.
The dialysis unit had faced a similar setback. Two of its five machines had broken down, restricting treatment. Repairs have restored all five machines, and the hospital plans to increase dialysis from two shifts a day to three.
The hospital has also tightened staff management. Employees now meet for half an hour before the 9am opening to review problems, assign responsibilities and address delays in patient care.
Hospital administration chief Lekhraj Katuwal said staff must arrive on time and complete their shifts. During handovers, outgoing staff cannot leave until replacements take over.
“We hold a meeting and review operations before the office opens,” Katuwal said. “We discuss problems affecting service delivery and try to resolve them immediately.”
Rai said the hospital was also tackling internal disorder. “We are putting patients and the public at the centre of the hospital,” he said. “We are also working to remove disorder and unhealthy interference. We have come here to work. If something obstructs that work, we have to remove the obstruction.”
‘Better than before’
Patients say they have started to notice the changes.
Mishrilal Sada of Triyuga Municipality said the hospital feels better than it did in the past. Sita Basnet said patients previously faced long waits and often struggled to find doctors. She now sees doctors more regularly and finds the services easier to access. Maniram Puri said Rai himself visits patients, asks about their experience and monitors services.
Human rights activist Dilip Rasaili also said he had seen early improvements. “We have seen signs of improvement within the first few days,” Rasaili said. “The team working under the current leadership has created some hope that the hospital can improve.”
Capacity remains a problem
Udayapur Hospital still operates well beyond its designed capacity. The hospital has government approval for 50 beds but currently runs 94. It treats up to 500 outpatients a day.
Staffing remains another major constraint. Of 59 approved permanent positions, only 29 are filled. The hospital employs 156 people in total through the management committee, provincial contracts, scholarship schemes and daily-wage arrangements.
Much of its daily operation therefore depends on temporary staff.
The hospital has 13 specialist doctors but only five medical officers, against a requirement of at least eight. It also needs more nurses, health assistants and other paramedics.
“The number of specialists is almost adequate, but we do not have enough medical officers,” Rai said. “Service delivery would be much easier if we had at least one medical officer for each specialist.”
An anaesthesiology specialist has recently joined the hospital.
The administration is also preparing to introduce electronic medical records, which it says will make it easier to maintain patient histories, retrieve reports and manage services.
It plans to add a third patient registration counter for older people, people with disabilities, pregnant women and other patients who need priority access. Another blood-sample collection centre is also planned, along with changes to the queue system.
The hospital says it is receiving medicines more regularly, but it still needs to complete the tender process for 98 medicines that it must provide free of charge.
The changes, therefore, have not resolved every problem. Patients still need medicines, tests and treatment to be available when they seek care.
Debt adds to the pressure
The hospital receives about Rs140 million to Rs150 million a year from the federal and provincial governments and generates another Rs100 million to Rs120 million from internal sources, according to the administration. It nevertheless carries liabilities of about Rs27.5 million.
Rai said the hospital would try to stop financial leakages and clear its debts. The hospital will also need to make its finances more transparent, particularly over the size and nature of its liabilities and how previous administrations managed its income and spending.
Resistance inside the hospital
Hospital administrators say the reform effort has met resistance. They accuse some groups of trying to force leadership changes, build factions among employees, create disputes and undermine staff who are supporting the reforms.
The administration also says some employees appointed under political pressure have resisted instructions and contributed to factionalism. Those allegations have not been independently verified. Residents, however, say sustained improvement will require stable leadership and believe the management team should be given at least two years to work without disruption.
Plans for a regional referral centre
The Koshi provincial government plans to develop Udayapur Hospital as a referral centre for Udayapur and neighbouring Khotang, Bhojpur, Okhaldhunga, Saptari and Siraha districts. The plan includes intensive care, a neonatal intensive care unit, a burn unit and a geriatric ward.
Rai said the hospital could make substantial progress within two years if the reform effort continues without interference.
For a hospital whose services had become increasingly unreliable, reopening basic units and enforcing workplace discipline are modest steps. But after years of complaints, they are also the first visible signs that Udayapur Hospital may be able to rebuild the public confidence it lost.

title: ‘De kinderen vonden het leuk om even met iets anders bezig te zijn’
content:
‘De kinderen vonden het leuk om even met iets anders bezig te zijn’
Biedt context, achtergrond, uitleg of meer detail over een specifiek onderwerp
Het laatste dat fotograaf Lisa van den Berg (25) wilde, is dat de kinderen op haar foto’s er zielig uit zouden zien. Ze zijn wel ziek, net zoals zij was als kind. „In het ziekenhuis gaat het veel over jou, bijna niemand praat met jou. Ik deed dat wel, ik kwam voor hen.”
Zou je het zien als je het niet zou weten, wat de kinderen op deze foto’s delen? Dat ze iets hebben waardoor ze veel tijd in het ziekenhuis doorbrengen? Misschien niet, of het zou moeten zijn dat ze kwetsbaar lijken. Niet zwak, niet aan hun lot overgelaten. Meer alsof er iets is wat ze in hun eentje moeten dragen, ondanks alle liefde en zorg.
Ze zien er zeker niet zielig uit. En dat is ook het laatste dat fotograaf Lisa van den Berg (25) wil overbrengen met deze serie, waarop ze eerder dit jaar afstudeerde aan de kunstacademie in Den Haag. „Zieke mensen worden doorgaans afgebeeld als held óf als zielepiet, bleek uit mijn vooronderzoek. Dat komt niet overeen met mijn ervaring – ik ben als kind ook veel ziek geweest. De ene keer voel je je sterk, de andere keer niet. Je hebt een aandoening, die is er, daar moet je mee dealen.”
Haar serie borduurt voort op een project dat ze vier jaar geleden heeft gedaan, een aantal kinderen fotografeerde ze toen én nu. Eerst wilde ze de kinderen dit keer in het ziekenhuis fotograferen; uiteindelijk portretteerde ze hen zonder herkenbare omgeving, soms ook thuis, en maakte daarnaast stillevens in het Wilhelmina Kinderziekenhuis. Het effect is des te sterker: je gaat vanzelf bedenken dat deze kinderen dus elke dag die saaie stoelen zien, dat witte gordijn, die blauwe plastic handschoenen.
In het begin voelde ze zich soms wat bezwaard, zegt Van den Berg. „De kinderen zijn natuurlijk ziek, voelen zich niet lekker en dan kom je een foto van ze maken. Maar ik merkte dat ze het leuk vonden om even met iets anders bezig te zijn. In het ziekenhuis gaat het veel over jou, er wordt aan je gezeten, er worden testjes gedaan; bijna niemand praat met jou. Ik deed dat wel, ik kwam voor hen.” Haar eigen ervaringen met ziekenhuizen maakten het contact makkelijker, denkt ze. „Je deelt iets, je komt niet als buitenstaander even aapjes kijken. Daar wilde ik ver van blijven.”
De kinderen gingen verschillend met hun situatie om, zegt ze. „Dide was drie toen ik haar voor het eerst fotografeerde, een kindje dat niet beter wist dan dat dit het leven is. Een jongen, Bram, is nu zestien, in de puberteit – dan wil je niet ziek zijn.”
Van den Berg had als kind eczeem, astma en jeugdreuma. Ze werd daarvoor nooit opgenomen, maar kwam tussen haar tweede en elfde jaar heel vaak in verschillende ziekenhuizen, lange tijd een of twee keer per week. ‘Het ziekenhuis’ werd een soort tweede thuis, al zou ze het, zegt ze, nooit zo hebben genoemd. „Maar ik wist precies: vanaf de ingang linksaf, rechtsaf… nu nog kan ik me de routes precies voor de geest halen. Het hele ziekenhuis zit in je hoofd.”
Sommige van haar interieurfoto’s zijn opzettelijk overbelicht. „Het begon met een testfoto waarbij een lamp te hard stond. Bij het terugkijken kreeg ik daar een herinnering bij, een gevoel van wel aanwezig zijn maar wat afgezonderd, wegdwalend in je koppie. Dat overbelichte, het half wel half niet zien, symboliseert voor mij dat gevoel.”
Haar realiteit is intussen een andere. „Rond mijn elfde kregen mijn ouders de keus tussen doorbehandelen of even niks doen. Ze kozen voor het laatste. Dat, naast de hormoonveranderingen in de puberteit, heeft ervoor gezorgd dat ik ‘eroverheen gegroeid’ ben. Ik ben nu een gezonde vrouw, geen ziek kind meer.”

title: Menina atacada por abelhas tem alta após uma semana e mais de 100 picadas em MG; vídeo
content:
Menina atacada por abelhas tem alta após uma semana e mais de 100 picadas em MG; vídeo
Que notícia boa: a menina Safira Emanuele Gomes dos Santos Rosa, de 12 anos, que sofreu ataque de abelhas, recebeu alta do hospital nesta segunda-feira (21), uma semana depois de sofrer mais de 100 picadas em Ibirité, na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte (MG). A menina precisou ficar no CTI pediátrico depois do resgate feito pelo motoboy Vinícius Martins de Paulo, o Vinny.
A alta da menina foi confirmada durante entrada ao vivo da reportagem da RecorTV Minas, nesta segunda, 21, quando a Safira já estava com a mochila dela nas costas para deixar o hospital.
Um dia antes da alta, ela apareceu pela primeira vez em vídeo e tranquilizou quem acompanhava a recuperação dela. “Tô muito bem. Muito obrigada pelas mensagens positivas e pelo carinho”, disse a estudante no sábado (19).
Relembre o caso
O Só Notícia Boa mostrou na última quarta-feira (16) o momento em que a Safira foi salva pelo Vinny.
Ele entrou no meio do enxame, usou o desodorante que carregava no bagageiro da moto para dipersar as abelhas e levou cerca de 40 ferroadas durante o socorro.
No dia seguinte, ele ganhou um carro e uma moto pela boa ação do grupo Tropa do Bem.

As picadas que ela teve
Safira chegou a ficar internada no CTI pediátrico por causa da quantidade de ferroadas. As picadas atingiram principalmente rosto, cabeça e pescoço, além da boca e da língua.
Na sexta-feira (18), a família recebeu a notícia de que os exames haviam melhorado e que a menina não corria mais risco de desenvolver arritmia cardíaca ou insuficiência renal em decorrência do ataque. Depois disso, ela deixou o CTI e seguiu para uma sala de observação.
Já no fim de semana, Safira contou que o inchaço havia diminuído bastante e que conseguia falar e comer melhor. Ela aguardava apenas uma nova avaliação médica para poder voltar para casa.
“Deus enviou ele para mim”
Em entrevista exibida pelo Fantástico neste domingo (20), Safira também falou sobre Vinícius e agradeceu ao motoboy que parou a moto para ajudá-la quando ela estava paralisada no meio do enxame.
“Deus ter enviado ele para mim foi a melhor coisa que aconteceu”, disse a menina.
Safira contou que, naquele momento, imaginou que poderia ficar no local sem que ninguém aparecesse para ajudá-la.
Uma semana depois do ataque
O ataque aconteceu na segunda-feira (14), quando uma colmeia caiu de uma árvore perto de uma escola no bairro Jardim Montreal, em Ibirité. O avô e a irmã mais nova de Safira também foram atingidos pelas abelhas.
Safira foi levada inicialmente para uma unidade de pronto atendimento e depois transferida para um hospital em Contagem, onde permaneceu sob acompanhamento médico durante a recuperação.
Agora, uma semana após o ataque, a menina atacada por abelhas finalmente pôde deixar o hospital e vai continuar a recuperação em casa.

title: Candidaturas de pessoas bissexuais, gays, lésbica, trans e pansexual ganham visibilidade nas eleições de 2026 no Rio Grande do Sul
content:
Pela primeira vez em uma eleição geral, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) disponibiliza no sistema DivulgaCandContas dados sobre a orientação sexual declarada pelas candidaturas.
No Rio Grande do Sul, 18 candidaturas registraram orientação sexual LGBTQIAPN+ nas eleições de 2026: oito pessoas bissexuais, oito gays, uma lésbica e uma pansexual. Outras quatro candidaturas utilizaram nome social. O número corresponde a 1,71% das 1.051 candidaturas registradas no estado. A maior concentração das candidaturas autodeclaradas está nos partidos do campo progressista e de esquerda (Psol, PT, UP, PCdoB e PDT), há registros também no MDB e PSDB.
Segundo levantamento da Aliança Nacional LGBTI+, o Rio Grande do Sul teve 31 candidaturas nas eleições de 2022, terceiro maior número entre os estados brasileiros.
Entre as 10 candidaturas trans registradas no Rio Grande do Sul pelo TSE no atual pleito, cinco são para deputado federal e cinco para deputado estadual. Por partido, o Psol registrou três candidaturas e o PT, duas, enquanto as demais estão distribuídas individualmente entre outras legendas (UP, MDB, PCdoB, PDT e PSDB).
Já o levantamento independente da Associação Nacional de Travestis e Transexuais (Antra), que acompanha candidaturas e campanhas de pessoas trans em todo o país, identificou 12 candidaturas trans no Rio Grande do Sul.
Entre os nomes que disputam as eleições de 2026 estão: Natasha Ferreira (PT), candidata a deputada estadual; Atena Beauvoir Roveda (Psol), candidata a deputada federal; Fabiane Gomes, a Faby Gomes (Psol), candidata a deputada estadual; Giovani Culau (PCdoB), candidato a deputado estadual; Rafael Dias Perlasca (Psol), candidato a deputado federal; Fabielly de Oliveira Teixeira, conhecida como Fabielly Klimberg (PSDB), candidata a deputada federal; e Daiana Santos (PCdoB), que concorre à reeleição para a Câmara dos Deputados.
No Legislativo municipal, as eleições de 2024 também marcaram uma mudança em Porto Alegre. A capital gaúcha elegeu a primeira bancada LGBTQIA+ da Câmara Municipal, formada por Atena Beauvoir Roveda (Psol), Natasha Ferreira (PT) e pelo mandato coletivo liderado por Giovani Culau (PCdoB). Ao todo, cinco vereadores que se identificam como LGBTI+ foram eleitos, distribuídos nessas três representações.
Para Ella Brites, cientista social e mestranda do Programa de Pós-Graduação em Ciência Política da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (PPGCP/UFRGS), o aumento das candidaturas pode sinalizar dois movimentos complementares: a abertura da arena pública para novas sujeitas políticas e o acirramento das disputas ideológicas, sobretudo por meio das ofensivas antigênero e antitrans.
Abertura da arena pública e ofensiva antigênero
Segundo Brites, pessoas e movimentos da dissidência sexual e de gênero passaram a agenciar o debate público a ponto de, em diferentes espectros ideológicos, surgirem alas da diversidade e temas ligados à comunidade em diferentes instâncias da arena pública, tanto no sentido da afirmação de direitos quanto dos ataques neoconservadores.
A cientista social considera razoável pensar que os movimentos sociais, a ocupação do espaço público, as estratégias de incidência política, a produção de conhecimento e a presença visível de pessoas LGBTQIAPN+, especialmente nas mídias e nos produtos comunicacionais, criaram um ambiente no qual essas existências ganharam outras possibilidades de significado. “Essa conjuntura cria as condições para a elaboração de uma imaginação política onde travestis negras são deputadas ou futuras presidentas do Brasil, por exemplo”, frisa.
Ao mesmo tempo, a pesquisadora aponta o fortalecimento da ofensiva neoconservadora. Para ela, o que foi ensaiado nas iniciativas “contra a ideologia de gênero” se aperfeiçoou na contemporânea ofensiva antitrans, com inúmeras legislações e propostas de lei circulando pelo país, fenômeno que também pode ser observado em países onde a extrema direita teve sucesso eleitoral, como os Estados Unidos.
Esse acirramento, pontua Brites, convoca sujeitas dos movimentos sociais a traçar estratégias de enfrentamento e resistência ao desmonte de direitos conquistados e de políticas públicas acumuladas. Ela observa que, ao serem colocadas como “inimigas da nação”, por “perturbar a ordem familiar da sociedade”, essas pessoas acabam sendo colocadas em evidência.
A cientista social pondera que a população brasileira e gaúcha não é LGBTfóbica “de modo geral e indiscriminado”. No limite, afirma, as pessoas reproduzem LGBTfobia de modo mais ou menos consciente, embora a população possua “traços conservadores marcantes”.
Os casos de candidaturas LGBTQIAPN+ aos Executivos, avalia, ainda são restritos e, em linhas gerais, distantes de ter essa pauta como centralidade. Nas eleições majoritárias, para prefeito, governador, presidente e Senado, segundo ela, pessoas da comunidade são consideradas “eleitoralmente fracas”, tendo como principal justificativa o suposto conservadorismo da população.
Brites chama atenção para os interesses dos partidos. O eleitorado, afirma, é visto como um “mercado a ser disputado”, o que favorece a presença, mesmo que diminuta e ausente de propostas políticas oriundas dos movimentos sociais LGBTQIAPN+, de pessoas da comunidade em diferentes siglas partidárias, com o objetivo de disputar os votos desse eleitorado. “Cabe salientar, para concluir, que pessoas LGBTQIAPN+ são livres para aderir à perspectiva político-partidária que lhes convier.”
Representatividade ainda distante da proporcionalidade
Conforme observa a cientista política, ainda existe muita incerteza sobre o quantitativo de pessoas LGBTQIAPN+ na sociedade. Ela relaciona isso à peculiaridade da identificação e à possibilidade de não publicização dela, quando existe essa possibilidade. Esse cenário, avalia, lança dúvidas sobre a proporcionalidade da representação da comunidade na política institucional. “De modo geral, até onde se sabe, somos um quantitativo baixo, proporcionalmente falando.”
A questão da baixa presença LGBTQIAPN+ na política institucional, porém, ressalva Brites, vem de outro lugar. Apesar do cenário de avanço e abertura às pessoas e pautas da dissidência sexual e de gênero nas arenas públicas e institucionais, a resistência à presença dessas pessoas ainda organiza muitas dessas ambiências.
De acordo com a pesquisadora, em todos os espectros ideológicos há registros, públicos ou não, de dificuldades com as pautas da dissidência sexual e de gênero. Essas dificuldades, afirma, podem não inviabilizar essas pautas, mas condicioná-las de modo a atender aos grupos dirigentes e seus interesses eleitorais.
Outro aspecto fundamental, aponta, é a própria condição para a ocupação política. “Disputar uma eleição exige muita estrutura, muito apoio, muito amparo.”
Pessoas LGBTQIAPN+, sobretudo trans e não-bináries, já enfrentam, prossegue Brites, em linhas gerais, muitos desafios para estruturarem suas vidas pessoais. Estruturar uma vida política institucional, portanto, seria ainda mais desafiador. “Como podemos falar em maior presença política institucional se mal conseguimos postos de trabalho dignos?”, questiona.
Para a cientista social, uma reflexão interseccional envolve justamente a disposição de compreender quais camadas situam uma pessoa na malha social e quais dificuldades são potencializadas em função de seu corpo, de sua cor e de sua origem.
Coalizões e disputa de narrativas
Questionada sobre como ampliar a transformação da presença LGBTQIAPN+ nas instituições em propostas e políticas concretas, Brites afirma que “não há uma fórmula mágica”. As instituições, segundo ela, ainda estão se aprimorando constantemente em seu quotidiano, assim como os agentes políticos.
A presença de pessoas LGBTQIAPN+ nas instituições políticas, não apenas em cargos eletivos, mas também por meio de nomeação e concurso, pontua a pesquisadora, não se traduz automaticamente em mais propostas ou pautas aprovadas ou encampadas.
Nesse processo, ela considera fundamental a formação de coalizões. “Nenhuma pauta, em qualquer ambiente institucional, fica em pé sozinha. Há que se ter muitos braços, e, eventualmente, muito fôlego, para construir o engajamento necessário à realização de determinado assunto.”
Particularmente, Brites acredita que um dos caminhos seja exercitar a imaginação política. A pesquisadora defende apostar na resposta rápida e eficaz das instituições quando tensionadas pelos movimentos sociais e pela opinião pública, ao mesmo tempo em que são implementadas estratégias de incidência política qualificada. Essa, segundo ela, é a experiência acumulada até agora, “com alguns frutos”.
A cientista social considera urgente retirar a comunidade LGBTQIAPN+ do lugar de “inimiga pública da nação”, de “perversidão da ordem natural e divina da família e dos bons costumes”. Para isso, acredita, é necessário disputar a narrativa.
Essa disputa, ressalta, não se resume a postagens em redes sociais. Envolve apostar em pessoas LGBTQIAPN+ como lideranças, encontrar formas de não precarizar suas existências e não tratar a pauta LGBTQIAPN+ como “perfumaria para agradar um setor eleitoral”.
Também envolve, segundo ela, celebrar “com calor, iconografia e paixão” as vidas LGBTQIAPN+, transformando antes a paisagem simbólica e o avesso das instituições.
Brites critica uma lógica institucional em que as pessoas calculam as melhores estratégias de sucesso sem contar no horizonte com algo diferente de “um homem cis branco heteronormativo (mesmo que não seja heterossexual)”.
“Habitar as brechas”
Sobre como ampliar a participação LGBTQIAPN+ na política, Brites responde que seria necessária, no limite, uma transformação muito profunda da sociedade. Em termos atuais, porém, considera que existem formas de estar e disputar os espaços de acordo com as possibilidades de cada realidade.
Mais uma vez, ela aponta a importância das coalizões. Seja uma candidatura, um mandato ou uma organização social LGBTQIAPN+, a proposta, afirma, fica mais interessante quando fala “diferentes línguas” e dialoga com diferentes pautas e setores da sociedade.
A pesquisadora cita como exemplo a deputada Erika Hilton, que, segundo ela, tem emplacado conquistas legislativas e políticas que, num plano geral, contemplam a comunidade LGBTQIAPN+, mas não se limitam a ela.
Brites avalia que o Brasil e o Rio Grande do Sul são “muito hostis” à comunidade LGBTQIAPN+. Para ela, essa hostilidade não é por acaso: o arranjo social teria sido desenhado para comportar e beneficiar, de modo geral, homens cis brancos heteronormativos. “Alguém ganha com isso.”
Ao mesmo tempo, ela não acredita que seja necessário “convencer” a sociedade como um todo de que pessoas LGBTQIAPN+ são “pessoas legais e dignas de representar a todes na política”. “O caminho é seguir habitando as brechas, é seguir dinamizando a disputa, é fazer o possível com o que dá e seguir cobrando por mais.”
Para Brites, imaginar a imposição de um grande consenso social flerta com um repertório quase fascista de uma sociedade “coesa e coerente”. Por isso, considera importante estimular a discordância e a existência de pontos de vista distintos.
O que deve ser evitado, segundo ela, são os repertórios violentos que habitam o “lençol freático” da política. Isso, afirma, pode ser feito com vulnerabilidade, exposição, ativismo institucional, estratégias localizadas caso a caso e políticas de cuidado, eventualmente, com mudanças de rota da vida política. “A luta por tornar o espaço da política mais habitável para a dissidência sexual e de gênero é uma luta por ampliar o espaço da humanidade, da vida digna.”
Na avaliação da pesquisadora, essa luta extrapola as questões conjunturais, pois diz respeito, “feliz ou infelizmente”, aos últimos mil anos da história do Ocidente.

title: Gossas : Clôture des 72H de l'Emploi, le Gouvernement réaffirme son engagement auprès des jeunes et des femmes
content:
Gossas : Clôture des 72H de l'Emploi, le Gouvernement réaffirme son engagement auprès des jeunes et des femmes
Présidant ce lundi 21 septembre 2026 la cérémonie de clôture des « 72H de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle et technique » dans la commune de Gossas, le ministre Idrissa Samb s'est félicité des résultats obtenus sur le terrain. Accompagné de Marie Angélique Diouf, ministre de la Famille et des Solidarités, ainsi que des autorités locales, il a réaffirmé sa conviction que « l’accès à l’emploi et aux compétences doit se faire au plus près des réalités territoriales ».
Portée par la Direction de l'Emploi et le 3FPT, cette initiative s'est traduite par des actions directes en faveur des jeunes, des femmes et des entreprises de la localité. Lors de ces trois jours de mobilisation, les équipes n'ont « pas seulement dialogué : elles ont agi ». Le bilan affiche notamment « 167 demandeurs d’emploi profilés et orientés », « 51 entreprises prospectées », dont « 14 entreprises d'ores et déjà enrôlées dans la Convention Nationale État-Employeurs (CNEE) ».
L'autonomisation des femmes et l'insertion des jeunes ont également occupé une place centrale avec « 800 femmes formées », « 20 GIE financés, bénéficiant directement à un ensemble de 300 femmes », et « 107 ASC touchées à l’échelle du département grâce au déploiement du programme “1 ASC, 1 métier” ».
L'événement s'est achevé par la mise en place d'une structure pérenne : « une Mission locale pérenne, installée pour faire vivre cet élan au quotidien ». Ce nouveau guichet de proximité a été pensé pour « accueillir, guider et propulser nos jeunes demandeurs d’emploi ainsi que l'ensemble des porteurs de projets », dans le cadre d'un déploiement qui va se poursuivre sur tout le territoire national.

title: He slept hungry in Bengaluru. Now he is lifeline for city’s migrant workers
content:

When a migrant worker in Bengaluru hits a wall – an employer refusing to pay months of wages, an eviction notice issued without warning, an unaffordable hospital emergency, or a police complaint that is not taken seriously – one of the first calls they often make is to R Kaleemullah. Migrants across the city reach out to him when they do not know where else to turn. He may not be able to solve every problem himself, but he usually knows someone who can help.
At 51, Kaleemullah is the national vice-president of the labour union All India Shramik Swaraj Kendra. Over more than three decades in Bengaluru, he has built a network of lawyers, trade unionists, social workers and grassroots volunteers who can be called on when a worker needs help. He can be found at police stations, hospital corridors, government offices and in the crowded settlements where migrant workers live.
For the workers who turn to him, his credibility stems not only from his work but also from his own experience of living with uncertainty.
“I never planned to become a social worker,” Kaleemullah says. “But when you have lived through extreme vulnerability yourself, you recognise the pain immediately in someone else. You understand what it feels like to be completely helpless.”
Kaleemullah grew up in a small rural hamlet in Andhra Pradesh. Even as a child, he questioned what he felt was unfair. When he was 12, he questioned village elders about funds collected for religious events that he believed had not been accounted for properly. The dispute escalated. A complaint was filed against him, and he was taken to the local police station and beaten, he recalls.
His father, too, challenged what he considered arbitrary decisions by authorities. Around the same time, he objected to a municipal tax of Rs 700 imposed on a computer they had bought. He refused to pay, leading to a legal battle that continued for nearly 12 years. During this period, municipal authorities repeatedly cut the family’s water and power connections, and their small poultry business was also affected.
Around 1990, an illness ended his formal education. After recovering from severe jaundice, Kaleemullah returned to school, but the headmaster demanded an unauthorised re-admission fee of Rs 500. His father refused to pay. Kaleemullah did not return to the classroom.
With only a Class 10 certificate, he left his village in 1991 to look for work. He first went to Hyderabad, where he trained in air-conditioner and refrigerator repair, hoping to find a job in the Gulf eventually. When that plan did not work out, he moved to Mumbai and took up temporary wage jobs. He later boarded a train to Bengaluru, intending to enrol in a technical diploma course.
But survival in the city soon took priority over his studies. He cleaned domestic refrigerators in residential neighbourhoods for Rs 5 a day. Food was often difficult to afford. “A few friends and I would soak cotton cloths in water and tie them tightly around our stomachs to reduce hunger,” he says.
There were also days when he could not afford the bus fare. On one occasion, he says, he bought a bus ticket to learn the route and then walked the same route to work every day.
By the mid-1990s, he found steady work at a garment shop in Shivajinagar. He started on a daily wage of Rs 60, which later rose to Rs 100. The job gave him a close look at the difficulties workers from outside the state faced. He saw workers facing extortion, being picked up by beat constables without explanation and losing wages without recourse. He also saw Dalit and minority workers struggle to speak up, often because they did not know the local language or how to navigate the system.
His involvement began simply: he accompanied workers who needed help. Whenever a worker was assaulted or taken to a police station, Kaleemullah would go with them. He began sitting in on legal consultations, learning procedures and understanding how complaints and documents moved through government offices.
“My education came from living in the streets,” he says. “I have not studied many books, but I have spent years sitting with people during their worst moments. That is where I learnt how the law works, and how easily it can work against those who are poor.”
By 2002, Kaleemullah’s work had moved beyond helping workers with individual problems. He volunteered at relief camps after the Gujarat violence that year, joined campaigns with Dalit rights groups across Karnataka and worked with activists opposing the demolition of slum settlements.
Through Vimochana, a Bengaluru-based women’s rights organisation, he began assisting women in cases involving domestic violence, sexual assault and offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
During the Covid-19 pandemic, his network expanded significantly as volunteers and helpers reached out to people in need across the state. Many of those seeking assistance were migrant workers from Assam, Manipur, West Bengal, Mumbai, Tamil Nadu and other parts of the country. “Even today, if they face a problem or need help, they call me,” he says.
His work with women has also brought him into conflict with conservative sections of the communities he works with. He says men have threatened him for helping women find jobs, get education, or even open bank accounts.
“I see these women as my sisters,” he says. “When a woman comes to me after being assaulted, I cannot ask her religion or caste. An assault is an assault. If her dignity has been violated, I have to stand by her.”
One case in particular brought him strong opposition from a section of the community. A young woman from Hubballi approached him alleging that she had been sexually abused over a prolonged period by a local Islamic scholar. Kaleemullah and his team worked with the police, leading to the scholar’s arrest, he says. Following the arrest, some members of the community criticised him and called him a “kafir” and “gaddar” (traitor).
Another case that stayed with him involved the alleged sexual assault of a 10-year-old girl by a temple priest in Devanahalli in 2020. The priest was arrested and booked under the POCSO Act and has since been convicted.
For Kaleemullah, the two cases also reflect how his work can be viewed through the religious identity of the people involved. He says his interventions are sometimes questioned or given a communal colour, particularly when he works with Muslim migrant workers.
“A large number of sanitation workers, ragpickers and construction workers in Bengaluru are Bengali Muslims. When I stand up for their legal rights or question arbitrary detentions, people often look at me through their religious identity. But for me, the issue is the same whether the person seeking help is a Muslim, Hindu or from any other community,” he says.
Despite the difficulties he faced when he first arrived in the city, Kaleemullah says Bengaluru has eventually become a place where he has found support and a sense of purpose. “Bengaluru was hard on me in the beginning. But over the years, it has given me a lot of love, trust and purpose,” he says.
Over the past decade, Kaleemullah has also begun training young people who want to work with vulnerable communities. Students of social work, sociology and journalism have interned with him, accompanying him to informal labour settlements, police stations and labour commission hearings.
He tries to teach them how the system works on the ground: how to follow up on a complaint and understand the difficulties faced by workers and victims.
His work also extends to the children of migrant waste-pickers and construction workers. His volunteers identify children who have dropped out of school in informal settlements and help them learn so they can enrol in government schools.
“Without education, their children will go through the same struggles as their parents. Getting a child into school is the first step towards breaking that cycle”, he stresses.
His work has also come with personal risks. Over more than three decades of advocacy, Kaleemullah says he has received several death threats, particularly during wage disputes, anti-encroachment drives and disputes between communities.
His family has often asked him to step away from the work, especially after he suffered health problems and underwent major cardiac surgery. But he still takes calls from workers who need help.
“Even my family tells me to sit at home. But if I do not help them, who else will? When I came here, I had nobody either. I do not want people who have placed their hopes in me to feel betrayed,” he says.
He was recently awarded the Lifetime Achievement Award for the Society Support category by The Khazi India Foundation – 2026. The award recognises his work with migrant labourers, Adivasis and Dalits, victims of injustice and families affected by demolitions, along with his humanitarian work during the Covid-19 pandemic, legal aid and support for vulnerable families, peace-building during communal crises and efforts towards youth education and awareness.

title: Schon während OP - Dank neuer Technik Tumor in Rekordzeit durchschaut
content:
Muss am Gehirn operiert werden, ist das eine extrem heikle und sehr komplexe Aufgabe. In Innsbruck stehen den Medizinern nun Hilfsmittel zur Verfügung, die Unglaubliches können und in Rekordzeit wichtige Informationen liefern.
In Österreich erkranken jedes Jahr laut Adelheid Wöhrer von der Medizin-Uni Innsbruck rund 2000 Menschen an einem Gehirntumor. Dazu kommen rund 10.000 Krebspatienten mit Metastasenbildung im Kopf.
Eine Operation ist ein heikles Unterfangen, das Ärzten und Technik alles abverlangt. Geht es doch darum, krankes Gewebe vollständig zu entfernen, aber gesunde Areale unberührt zu lassen. Millimeterarbeit, für die an der Uni-Klinik in Innsbruck erstmals zwei Geräte mit außergewöhnlichen Fähigkeiten eingesetzt werden.
Noch während einer laufenden Operation erhalten wir die Diagnose, um welchen Tumor es sich handelt.
Christian Freyschlag, Neurochirurg
Bild: Christof Birbaumer
„Mit den neuen KI-gestützten Analysemethoden der NIO-Bildgebung und Nanopore-Sequenzierung wird die Wartezeit auf eine Diagnose für Patienten von zwei bis drei Wochen auf wenige Stunden bis Minuten verkürzt. So können viel früher die Weichen für die geeignete Therapie gestellt werden“, fasst Wöhrer, Leiterin des Instituts für Neuropathologie, zusammen. Besagte NIO-Bildgebung ermöglicht auch ein noch gezielteres Entfernen eines Tumors. „NIO erlaubt es uns, mittels Laser Art und Ausdehnung eines Tumors präzise darzustellen, sodass wir millimetergenau operieren können“, erläutert Neurochirurg Christian Freyschlag.
Am Institut für Neuropathologie der Medizin-Universität geht es dann mithilfe der Nanopore-Sequenzierung an die Analyse des Tumors. So können die Mediziner seine Gefährlichkeit besser einschätzen und daraufhin die Therapie sehr gezielt auf die betroffenen Patienten abstimmen.
Mit den neuen Analysemethoden können viel früher die Weichen für die geeignete Therapie gestellt werden.
Adelheid Wöhrer, Leiterin des Instituts für Neuropathologie
Bild: Christof Birbaumer
Für Patienten steigen die Überlebenschancen
In Summe ein Vorgehen, das in Zukunft auch bei anderen Tumorerkrankungen möglich sein wird. Eine enge Kooperation zwischen Tirol Kliniken und Med-Uni sei die Basis dafür, betonen Rektor Gert Mayer und Thomas Klestil, medizinischer Geschäftsführer der Tirol Kliniken.
In der Pilotphase wurden bereits rund hundert Eingriffe erfolgreich durchgeführt. Die Mediziner sehen damit die Überlebenschancen für Patienten weiter steigen.

title: Au Festival du Monde, la scène musicale devient une tribune pour les droits des femmes
content:
« Quand c’est non, dommage. Range ton crayon, ta plume sauvage. Quand c’est non, c’est non. » Sur scène, un piano noir soutient une voix douce, mais une voix en colère. Jeanne Cherhal fait partie des huit artistes réunis ce soir dans le cadre d’un concert inédit « Nos voix pour toutes x Le Monde », organisé sur le parvis du journal Le Monde, dans le 13e arrondissement parisien. L’événement est coorganisé par la Fondation des femmes, à qui l’intégralité des bénéfices sera reversée – une organisation reconnue qui apporte un appui financier, juridique et matériel aux associations de terrain venant en aide aux femmes victimes de violences et œuvrant pour l’égalité.
« En tant qu’artiste, j’ai la chance d’avoir une tribune et je pense qu’il faut savoir s’en saisir », confie Jeanne Cherhal. Pour elle, ce combat se mène par la colère, mais pas seulement : « Parfois, c’est par le rire qu’on arrive le mieux à faire passer des messages. J’aime qu’on qualifie mon féminisme de joyeux. A chacun sa façon de vivre son combat », lance l’artiste. Mais son sourire s’efface dès qu’elle évoque cette question d’un point de vue politique : « C’est à nous de pallier le manquement de l’Etat en matière de lutte contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles. Heureusement qu’en France, le tissu associatif est très développé et que les victimes peuvent compter dessus. »
Sur cette même scène, Nesrine fait chanter son violoncelle. Derrière les volants de sa robe noire, la chanteuse et violoncelliste franco-algérienne a ainsi choisi de ne s’entourer que de femmes pour les postes techniques qui l’accompagnent : « On ne peut pas faire comme si les inégalités de genre n’existaient pas. Les événements comme celui de ce soir sont un bon endroit pour se solidariser. »
Libertés nouvelles
Les femmes ne sont pas seules à se mobiliser ce soir-là. Youssef Swatt’s, jeune rappeur vainqueur de la saison 3 de « Nouvelle Ecole », est venu avec ses chansons et ses revendications. « J’essaye, à ma petite échelle, de me nourrir et de m’enrichir sur ces questions. Je suis convaincu que la musique est un des meilleurs moyens pour faire passer des messages. » Ce soir, il dédie son message à sa mère. A 60 ans, elle a claqué la porte du foyer familial et demandé le divorce. Elle a ensuite pris des cours de français et s’est battue pour une vie faite de libertés nouvelles. Elle a élevé son fils avec un dicton : « Patience, patience, tu iras au paradis. »
Ces années de patience, Youssef Swatt’s les a longtemps apprivoisées avec l’idée qu’une femme est une mère. « Il aura fallu que ces questions de féminisme et de liberté me touchent personnellement pour que je prenne conscience qu’une femme est une femme », souligne-t-il. Porté par ce qu’il appelle un sentiment de « vengeance » pour sa mère, il collabore à plusieurs reprises avec la Fondation des femmes. Depuis le jeudi 17 septembre, il a lancé une collecte de fonds : la vente de tee-shirts inspirés de la polémique que Pascal Praud avait déclenchée à son sujet en 2025, après qu’il avait tenu des propos contre l’extrême droite et le ministre de l’intérieur de l’époque, Bruno Retailleau. Les dons sont reversés à Human’s for Women, une association féministe intersectionnelle.
Le jeune rockeur Arthur Fu Bandini a lui aussi répondu présent : « Mes chansons parlent beaucoup de capitalisme. Mais pour moi, c’est lié : le capitalisme, c’est le patriarcat à l’état pur », explique-t-il. Chapeau de cuir, lunettes à verres jaunes, tee-shirt noir sans manches, le chanteur s’interroge aujourd’hui sur sa façon d’écrire : « Je me demande comment intégrer l’écriture inclusive dans mes morceaux. C’est important de réfléchir à ces questions, mais j’ai envie de bien faire les choses. Il faut être précis. »
Vient le dernier changement de décor. Cinq silhouettes prennent place dans la pénombre : guitare électrique, acoustique, piano, batterie, voix : Feu ! Chatterton s’installe sur scène. Dès les premières notes, des faisceaux bleus et roses traversent la foule. Mais peu à peu, les frontières cèdent et le public du festival gagne la scène, se glisse entre musiciens et instruments. Au milieu de cette marée humaine, le chanteur du groupe Arthur Teboul, les deux pieds sur une table, se fond dans la foule. Seul son micro permet encore de le distinguer. Ce soir-là, c’est pour toutes que Feu ! Chatterton a porté sa voix.

title: La Universidad Politécnica Territorial Andrés Eloy Blanco inscribió a 385 bachilleres en Carora durante un operativo especial en el municipio Torres
content:
Un total de 385 jóvenes provenientes de distintas parroquias del municipio Torres formalizaron su inscripción en la Universidad Politécnica Territorial Andrés Eloy Blanco (Uptaeb), durante un operativo de atención presencial llevado a cabo en las instalaciones del Liceo Egidio Montesinos, en Carora.
La jornada tuvo como propósito absorber a la población de aspirantes que permanecía en condición de rezagada por limitaciones de cupo en los Programas Nacionales de Formación (PNF) de Administración, Contaduría Pública, Agroalimentación y Ciencias de la Información.
María Alejandra Rodríguez, directora de Control de Estudio de la Uptaeb, explicó que el traslado de la directiva hacia la capital torrense responde a una política de descentralización para adaptar la capacidad instalada a la demanda real del interior del estado Lara. No obstante, admitió las limitaciones estructurales: "La universidad se queda corta ante la cantidad de bachilleres que desean ingresar. El límite no solo lo marca el espacio físico, sino la disponibilidad de docentes especialistas en cada área".
A la restricción de cupos se sumaron las fallas de servicios básicos durante el despliegue. La suspensión consecutiva de las dos fases eléctricas que surten al Liceo Egidio Montesinos obligó a habilitar una planta de combustión de emergencia para no paralizar la carga de datos en el sistema.
Por su parte, el coordinador de la Uptaeb en el municipio Torres, Freddy Campos, detalló que el operativo comenzó a las 8:00 am con aspirantes en fila desde las 6:00 am, cerrando la fase con la asignación final de 18 estudiantes en Contaduría y 13 en Administración. Campos puntualizó que la inestabilidad de la conectividad a internet complicó la digitalización de expedientes en formato PDF y la verificación del arancel de inscripción de 8.500 bolívares.
En el marco del programa de equiparación de oportunidades, la profesora Amarilis Rodríguez, adscrita a la Dirección de Políticas Estudiantiles, destacó que el abordaje incluyó la matriculación de estudiantes con discapacidad motora, intelectual y del espectro autista, a quienes se les asignó acompañamiento especial para el comienzo de clases programado para el 5 de octubre próximo.
La atención directa beneficia a bachilleres del casco urbano y de áreas rurales lejanas como la parroquia Cecilio Zubillaga en la población de La Pastora. Yixel Roa, residente del sector La Pastora e inscrita en el PNF de Administración, relató que anteriormente cursaba estudios en Barquisimeto, pero el costo recurrente del pasaje interurbano y las complicaciones logísticas la forzaron a desertar temporalmente.
Con la consolidación de estos 385 nuevos expedientes, la Uptaeb busca asegurar la permanencia de los jóvenes en su propia entidad geográfica, reduciendo la deserción universitaria provocada por el costo de movilización hacia la capital larense.

title: Edukativna radionica "Zdrava hrana svakog dana" i u novoj školskoj godini
content:
Foto: ANDREJ NIHIL / ANDREJ NIHIL X SIROVO Edukativna radionica "Zdrava hrana svakog dana" i u novoj školskoj godini autor: PR tekst Društvo 18. sep. 2026. 09:09 0 Podeli vest: Postavi Nova.rs za omiljeni Google izvor Više Interaktivna predavanja nutricioniste za učenike četvrtog razreda, koja su do sada održana u 337 osnovnih škola, od ovog septembra stižu u nove učionice širom Srbije. Podeli vest: Oglas Kroz zanimljive razgovore o pravilnoj i uravnoteženoj ishrani učenici u okviru Maxi programa edukacije „Zdrava hrana svakog dana“ uče o tome zašto je važno da se doručak ne preskače, povrće nađe u svakom obroku, voće bira za užinu, a hidratacija i fizička aktivnost budu neizostavan deo svakodnevice. Program edukacije, kroz koji je do sada prošlo više od 30.000 učenika četvrtih razreda, ove školske godine obići će osnovne škole u Sremskoj Mitrovici, Rumi, Inđiji, Pančevu, Vršcu, Zrenjaninu i Kovinu. Foto: Andrej Nihil / Maxi Programu „Zdrava hrana svakog dana“ prvi su ove godine prisustvovali četvrtaci Osnovne škole „Jovan Jovanović Zmaj“ iz Sremske Mitrovice. Oni su u razgovoru sa nutricionistom Ivanom Mišić podelili svoje dileme oko školske užine, zdravog doručka, ali i o tome koliko fizičke aktivnosti je važno imati tokom nedelje. „Veoma nam je drago što se naša škola našla u programu ’Zdrava hrana svakog dana’. Tema zdrave ishrane i pravilnog razvoja dece izuzetno je važna, a naši nastavnici se trude da u radu sa decom, uz redovan nastavni plan i program, što više pažnje posvećuju i ovim pitanjima. Zato se radujemo svakoj dodatnoj inicijativi koja decu edukuje i podstiče ih da razmišljaju o zdravijim izborima i navikama. Škola nije samo mesto gde se uče lekcije i dobijaju ocene, već i sredina u kojoj se oblikuju navike koje deca nose sa sobom kroz život. Verujem da ovakva predavanja mogu da budu važan podsticaj da ono što danas nauče sutra postane deo njihove svakodnevice“, istakla je Sonja Tucaković, direktorka OŠ „Jovan Jovanović Zmaj“. Maxi karavan „Zdrava hrana svakog dana“ pokrenut je 2023. godine uz podršku Ministarstva prosvete i ove školske godine ušao je u četvrtu godinu redovnih edukacija đaka u školama širom Srbije. „Do sada smo obišli škole u oko 70 gradova, opština i naselja, i svaki susret sa decom za nas je posebno inspirativan. Energija i entuzijazam četvrtaka u Sremskoj Mitrovici još jednom su nam pokazali koliko je važno da o ovim temama razgovaramo sa učenicima. Zdrave navike u ishrani i ljubav prema sportu svoje osnove grade još u detinjstvu. Zato ćemo i ove školske godine sa puno radosti biti sa učenicima u fiskulturnim salama i učionicama, razgovarati o zdravim navikama i zajedno učiti kako da ih gradimo i negujemo, dok ćemo njihove ideje i iskustva koristiti da ovaj program iz godine u godinu učinimo još boljim“, rekla je Milica Rakovac, ispred trgovinskog lanca Maxi. delhaize delhaize srbija maxi pr zdrava hrana Pratite nas na društvenim mrežama: Koje je tvoje mišljenje o ovoj temi? title: Brain Implant Lets a Paralyzed Patient Speak and Gesture at the Same Time
content:
A brain implant can now do something that wasn’t possible before. It can translate a person’s attempted words and gestures at the same time.
Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, tested the system in two people with severe paralysis. As the participants tried to speak, wave, nod or combine the two, the implant recorded activity from the brain’s movement centers and converted it into text and movements on a virtual avatar.
The challenge was that the brain did not produce exactly the same patterns when speech and gestures happened together as it did when each was attempted alone. A decoder trained only on isolated words or movements struggled with the combinations. It worked better once researchers trained it on both situations.
We all know that a conversation between two people is more than just the spoken word. The Italians, as they say, talk with their hands. As such, the whole idea behind this brain-computer interface is not just to restore a person’s words but also some semblance of their body language.
“Conversation is about much more than the words being spoken. It’s a multilayered, dynamic process involving the whole motor cortex,” Edward Chang, a neurosurgeon at the University of California, San Francisco, and senior author of the study, said in a statement. “This proof-of-concept shows us it’s possible for a BCI to restore some of this freedom and flexibility.”
More Than the Sum of Its Parts
The researchers enrolled three people with severe speech and/or movement impairments in UCSF’s BRAVO clinical trial. Two had experienced brainstem strokes; the third had amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS (the same disease Stephen Hawking had). Each person had a grid of 253 electrodes implanted on the surface of the left side of the brain, covering regions involved in speech and movement.
The main speech-and-gesture experiment involved two participants because the third withdrew before the full-body avatar experiments began. One participant, who had paralysis after a stroke, silently attempted five phrases and four gestures. The participant with ALS attempted 10 phrases while vocalizing and imagined 10 gestures, including waving, shrugging, and giving a thumbs-up. The researchers tested all 100 possible phrase-and-gesture combinations for this participant.
Some electrodes responded mainly to speech and others mainly to gestures. But many responded to both, particularly in the precentral gyrus—a strip of cortex involved in controlling movement. Speech activity tended to cluster farther down this region and gesture activity farther up, with a substantial area of overlap between them.
It’s precisely this overlap that has caused previous similar devices to fail. When researchers trained a machine-learning decoder only on speech performed alone or gestures performed alone, its performance suffered when participants tried both simultaneously.
Training it on examples of both isolated and simultaneous behavior worked better. The neural patterns evidently shifted enough during multitasking that the decoder needed to experience those contexts rather than assume that “speech plus gesture” was simply two independent signals laid on top of each other.
Encouragingly, the system could also decode speech-and-gesture combinations it had never encountered together during training. That’s a big plus for any future device as nobody could realistically train a BCI on every possible pairing of a word with a gesture.
From Words to a Whole Body
The researchers then connected the decoders to personalized full-body avatars. Intended speech appeared as text while decoded gestures made the avatar wave, clap, shrug, or perform other movements in real time.
During simultaneous testing in the participant with ALS, the system correctly classified speech 70% of the time and gestures 66% of the time. In a small conversational demonstration, those figures rose to 75 and 85%, respectively. The stroke participant reached 100% for both channels in conversational testing, although that result came from only three tiny blocks of trials.
Previously, in 2023, Chang’s group demonstrated a BCI that converted attempted speech into text, synthetic speech, and facial movements on an avatar. Other systems have restored cursor control and, more recently, generated synthetic speech almost instantaneously from brain activity. The new work pushes in a different direction: getting several forms of communication to coexist.
“But most of these studies have focused on restoring one of these functions at a time,” Samantha Brosler, a UCSF bioengineering researcher and study co-author, told Nature.
There are major caveats. The experiment involved only two people for simultaneous decoding, used tiny vocabularies and discrete gestures rather than free-flowing conversation, and relied on wires running from the implanted array to external equipment. The authors say larger vocabularies, continuous movements, and faster decoding remain future goals.
Still, the experiment suggests that restoring communication may eventually mean more than giving someone their words back. It could mean restoring body language.
The study was published in the journal Nature Neuroscience.

title: ANALAKELY - Les feux tricolores entrent en service
content: Nouveau repère pour les usagers à Analakely.Les feux tricolores installés à Analakely, en face de la Pharmacie de l’Océan Indien, sont désormais opérationnels. Placé à proximité d’un passage piéton, ce dispositif vise à sécuriser la traversée sur cet axe très fréquenté du centre-ville, où l’important flux de véhicules rend souvent le passage difficile.Lorsque le feu est rouge, les véhicules doivent s’arrêter pour laisser passer les piétons. Au vert, ils peuvent poursuivre leur route, tandis que les personnes à pied doivent attendre. Le feu jaune annonce le passage imminent au rouge et appelle les conducteurs à ralentir.« Nous avons parfois du mal à traverser, même en empruntant le passage piéton. Ces feux peuvent donc nous aider à passer plus facilement », témoigne un usager. Le dispositif devrait notamment profiter aux enfants, aux personnes âgées et aux personnes à mobilité réduite, qui ont besoin de davantage de temps pour traverser.L’efficacité du dispositif dépendra toutefois du comportement des usagers. Les conducteurs doivent s’arrêter avant le passage piéton et éviter de s’y immobiliser lorsque la circulation ralentit. Les piétons, de leur côté, sont appelés à attendre le signal leur permettant de traverser.Au-delà de la régulation des véhicules, ces feux introduisent de nouvelles habitudes dans cette partie d’Analakely. Leur respect devrait contribuer à fluidifier la circulation et à réduire les traversées désordonnées.Fanilo Mampianintsoa

title: $12 billion in Medicaid funds restored to Texas hospitals, ending impasse with the feds
content:
Nearly $12 billion in Medicaid funding to Texas hospitals will be restored, Gov. Greg Abbott said Thursday, ending a near year-long impasse between Texas and the federal government.
“This funding is a major victory for Texas patients,” Abbott said in a statement. “It authorizes nearly $12 billion for hospitals, physicians, rural clinics, nursing facilities, and behavioral health providers that serve patients in every region of our state. Emergency rooms will stay open, rural families will retain local care, and Texans will have access to the treatment they need. I thank CMS and the Trump Administration for helping ensure Texans get the medical care they need.”
The halt of the funds began on Sept. 1, the beginning of the state’s new fiscal year. It marked the first time the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services had stopped the supplemental funding to Texas hospitals since the funding began in 2014. It was not immediately clear when the funds would be transferred to Texas hospitals, which was slated to lose $27 million a day.
“We can breathe a little easier today. The Medicaid crisis hanging over our heads has been averted. We are deeply grateful to Gov. Abbott, state and federal leaders who listened, took our concerns seriously and acted with urgency to protect Texas patients,” said John Hawkins, president and CEO of the Texas Hospital Association. “Hospitals can focus on what they do best – saving lives and caring for Texans. Our gratitude cannot be overstated.”
Abbott’s announcement comes two weeks after The Texas Tribune reported that the governor’s office had stepped in last month, according to a letter he sent Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in which he called the move to hold onto the money an economic gun to Texas. The funding helps hospitals close the gap between their Medicaid reimbursements and the actual costs they incur for treating low-income Texans.
The dispute began late last year over questions about how Texas raises more than $4.2 billion in taxes to access those federal funds.
